translation.title: Clotrimazole Cream
translation.efficacy: This medicine is used for skin fungal infections caused by dermatophytes, yeast-like fungi and other fungi (ringworm, pityriasis versicolor, skin candidiasis, candidal vulvitis and candidal balanitis), for skin conditions with superinfection by these fungi, and for erythrasma caused by Corynebacterium.
translation.usage: Apply a thin layer to the affected area 2 to 3 times a day and rub it in. The treatment period varies with the severity and location of the condition: about 3 to 4 weeks for skin fungal infections, 1 to 3 weeks for pityriasis versicolor, 2 to 4 weeks for erythrasma, and 1 to 2 weeks for candidal vulvitis and candidal balanitis. To obtain a complete treatment effect, use it regularly for a sufficient period.
translation.caution: Do not use this medicine if you are or have been hypersensitive to it, to imidazole derivatives or to cetostearyl alcohol, or in children aged 2 or under. Before using it, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are pregnant or may become pregnant, or if you are breastfeeding. Follow the prescribed directions and dosage. Change towels, clothes and socks that touch the affected area every day. Before using this medicine, wash the affected area so that skin flakes are removed, leave no moisture, and dry completely, especially between the toes if you have athlete's foot. Do not use an occlusive dressing or wrapping unless directed by a doctor. Do not use acidic soap. When this medicine is applied to the genitals (women: the labia and around the vulva; men: the foreskin and glans), it may reduce the safety and effectiveness of latex products such as condoms and vaginal suppositories. This medicine is for external use only; do not swallow it. Do not use it in the eyes, on the cornea or conjunctiva, or on severe erosions. When using this medicine, it may weaken the action of topically applied amphotericin B and polyene antibiotics. Stop use immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist if adverse reactions occur, such as angioedema, anaphylactic reactions, hypersensitivity, low blood pressure, fainting, difficulty breathing, blisters, contact dermatitis, red spots, abnormal sensations, skin peeling, itching, a rash, hives, skin tingling, a burning feeling of the skin, or irritation at the application site.
